Concurrency guard middleware. Caps concurrent in-flight requests and rejects excess load early.

The cap is PER WORKER: under runCluster/runThreaded each process/thread owns its own ConcurrencyGuardState, so the effective global cap is workers * maxInflight. Divide maxInflight by the worker count for a global cap.

state is immutable-after-construction: maxInflight must not change after the middleware is built (it is read on the hot path without atomics). Passing state = nil allocates a fresh state on EVERY factory call, so call the factory once at app setup and register that single instance (registering the same state in two instances double-counts each request and halves the effective cap).

An empty contentType does not omit the Content-Type header: res.send falls back to the framework default (text/plain; charset=utf-8), so "" cannot mean "no Content-Type".

Counter ops use moAcquireRelease (stronger than the moRelaxed the limit logic requires) deliberately, for consistency with tryAcquireAsyncSlot in app.nim.

    ...raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Safe at any time: it is a no-op while any request is in flight (the CAS only succeeds while the counter is exactly 0, so a concurrent admission cannot be clobbered), and an in-flight completion cannot drive the counter negative after a reset.
